reason: The wording has not been compared with the translation it names, and this is the one line of the four where that matters. The verifier's own evidence concedes the printed page was not seen; the whole warrant is a single secondary witness, Bokser's block quote ending '(75)'. I read the Bokser PDF and it does support what she claims: her works cited lists 'Juana Ines de la Cruz. The Answer/La Respuesta. Including a Selection of Poems. Ed. Electa Arenal and Amanda Powell. New York: Feminist Press at the City University of New York, 1994', and her block quote runs 'It was well put by Lupercio Leonardo that one can philosophize quite well while preparing supper. I often say, when I make these little observations, "Had Aristotle cooked, he would have written a great deal more." (75)'. But one article is not the page, and this sentence is exactly the translation-drift trap the brief warns about: it circulates in at least four English renderings, and a post-1999 one shares the tail the line turns on. Edith Grossman, in Selected Works (Norton), reads 'And seeing these minor details, I say that if Aristotle had cooked, he would have written a great deal more' (quoted at p. 110 in the UNAM Mexican philosophy lecture); Pamela Kirk Rappaport (Paulist Press, 2005) reads 'As I often say on observing these little things, if Aristotle had cooked, he would have written much more' (printed in full at Lapham's Quarterly with the Paulist Press permission line); Margaret Sayers Peden reads 'had Aristotle prepared victuals, he would have written more'. A composite of Arenal and Powell's 'Had Aristotle cooked' with Grossman's 'a great deal more' would look exactly like the shipped line, and nothing I could reach rules that out. I tried: every search for the distinctive framing clause 'when I make these little observations' returns Bokser and nothing else; the archive.org copies of both the 1994 edition (answerlarespuest00sorj, answerincludings0000juan) and the 2009 expanded edition are lending restricted and the search-inside endpoints return no hit for the phrase; the Google Books API is over its daily quota. Two lesser faults. The theme fit is the weakest of the four: the kitchen and Aristotle is a line about knowledge in ordinary work, not about renewal or the road, in a month whose theme is Renewal and the Way. And the shipped quotation's last character is a closing quote mark rather than the full stop rule 32 asks for, because it nests a quotation inside the card's own quotation. Everything else is clean: the attribution is genuinely Sor Juana's and is not in the misattribution list, shipped.js returns no match, no near match, Sor Juana at 0 of 3, not banned, the tag Correspondence is right for the Respuesta, the scope and publishability are fine, and the source is 127 characters with no dash. Refuted on evidence, not on authorship: it can ship the moment someone opens page 75 of the 1994 Feminist Press text and confirms the sentence, or recites it to a translation whose page can actually be read. The editor should also weigh that this is the only woman of the four, so dropping it costs the month against the eight-women floor.
